changes.comment: createHttpTransport takes an optional fetch (McpFetch), and every HTTP request the session makes — each POST, the standalone GET event stream and the termination DELETE — goes through it. Pass SaferFetch.createGuardedFetch with blockPrivateNetworks() from @fgv/ts-extras to give MCP egress the same SSRF protection as other safer-fetch calls; without it, globalThis.fetch is used with no protection. A guarded fetch's refusal classifies as the new 'egress-blocked' McpFailureReason, carrying only the refusal's kind; its headers timeout classifies as 'timeout' (size the guarded fetch's headersTimeoutMs to your longest MCP request timeout — a JSON-response server holds a slow tool call's headers), and its network, aborted and internal failures as before; a refused DELETE is logged at detail and the close still resolves within its bound. Every egress refusal is also logged at detail by its kind only, never its URL — including one no operation waits on, such as the standalone event stream or the OAuth discovery the SDK runs after a 401 on its background reconnect.
